analysis.title: Mind on the Market: Treasury Supply and the Fed's Balance Sheet (Chart of the Week)
key_insights: Treasury issuance has tilted toward bills, where demand has stayed deep, rather than longer-dated securities that require investors to absorb more interest-rate risk.

Notes with 2 to 10 year maturities remain the largest component of publicly held debt, but their share has trended lower. The bill share rose sharply in 2020, retraced, and has moved higher since 2023.
Treasury added 6-week, 2-month and 4-month bills to its menu of short-dated securities over the past decade.
Treasury auction sizes have grown much faster for bills than for longer-dated securities, so a disproportionate share of recent financing growth has occurred at the front of the curve.

TBAC describes bills as shock absorbers that let Treasury adjust to changing financing needs without abrupt changes to coupon auction sizes. TBAC reported that recent bill supply increases met robust demand from money market funds, households and businesses.

If the marginal buyer is more willing to absorb short-term paper than longer-dated debt at prevailing yields, Treasury may have less flexibility to extend its funding mix without offering greater yield compensation.

Federal Reserve research finds bill supply can pull cash out of repo, and coupon issuance raises dealer financing needs. Both channels put upward pressure on repo rates, and repo rates become more sensitive to Treasury supply as reserves become less abundant.
In late 2025, with declining reserves and heavy Treasury issuance, overnight repo rates rose and stayed above the effective fed funds rate. SOFR traded above fed funds more frequently.
In December 2025 the FOMC determined reserve balances had declined to the ample range and told the New York Fed to begin reserve management purchases, conducted primarily in Treasury bills.

If heavy issuance keeps pressuring short-term funding markets as reserves get scarcer, controlling overnight rates may require a larger Fed balance sheet than otherwise. Fiscal financing choices can therefore affect the liquidity the Fed must provide.

State Street prefers defensive short-rate positioning and selective duration additions over large fixed-duration exposure at current levels. It says a more attractive entry point for duration could emerge at materially higher yields.

macro_indicators.indicator: Increase in 12-month average US Treasury bill auction size over the past 5 years
macro_indicators.interpretation: Bill auction sizes have grown far faster than total Treasury debt, which rose 41% over the same period.

macro_indicators.indicator: Increase in total US Treasury debt over the past five years
macro_indicators.interpretation: Borrowing needs keep growing, and the financing mix is shifting toward bills.

trade_ideas.description: Defensive short-rate positioning with selective duration additions, avoiding large fixed-duration exposure at current yields
trade_ideas.rationale: Until investors are compensated for absorbing more long-term Treasury supply, the balance of risks argues for caution on duration.

risk_factors: Rising Treasury supply could pressure short-term funding markets and repo rates as reserves become less abundant.
Extending borrowing further out the curve requires investors to absorb more duration risk and could require higher yield compensation.
Persistent SOFR deviations above fed funds could interfere with the Fed's control of short-term rates.
charts_described: Chart of the Week plots Treasury bills, bonds, notes, TIPS and floaters in trillions of dollars alongside bills, bonds and notes as a share of total public Treasury debt, showing bills playing a growing role in the funding mix.
Figure 3 plots SOFR against the effective fed funds rate from February 2024, showing SOFR moving above fed funds more frequently in late 2025.
vol_and_positioning: SOFR traded above the effective fed funds rate more frequently in late 2025, which the report reads as repo funding pressure reaching the Fed's policy-rate framework.
Persistent SOFR deviations from fed funds can signal that funding-market pressure is interfering with the Fed's implementation of policy.

tension_points.bull_case: Bills give Treasury flexible funding into deep demand from money market funds, households and businesses, and act as shock absorbers without abrupt coupon auction changes.
tension_points.bear_case: The widening gap between bill and coupon issuance suggests market capacity to absorb debt is not uniform across the curve. Longer-dated issuance would require more duration risk and greater yield compensation, and heavy bill supply can pressure repo and enlarge the Fed's balance sheet needs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Investors being sufficiently compensated for absorbing more long-term Treasury supply, with a more attractive duration entry point potentially emerging at materially higher yields.

theme_stances.key_argument: Heavy front-end issuance can complicate the Fed's control of short-term rates and leaves duration unattractive until yields compensate for supply.
theme_stances.evidence: the balance of risks argues for a cautious approach to duration

theme_stances.evidence: Fiscal financing decisions can therefore affect the liquidity the Fed must provide
